semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {هَلْ أتى}: There are two views on this «هل». The first: that it is used in its proper sense of pure interrogation, i.e. he is among those who are asked about because of the strangeness of his case: "Has there come upon him a period of time in which he was not such-and-such?" The answer would then be: "Yes, that came upon him, and he was in the state mentioned." So said al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], but it is open to objection, as you will shortly learn. Makkī said, establishing that it is used in its proper interrogative sense: "The best view is that it is in its proper sense of interrogation whose meaning is taqrīr (affirmation by questioning); it is an affirmation directed at the one who denies the resurrection, who must therefore say: 'Yes, a long age has passed in which there was no human being.' It is then said to him: 'He who brought him into being after he was not, and made him exist after his non-existence, how could the resurrection and the giving of life after death be impossible for Him?' That is the meaning of His saying: {وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النشأة الأولى فَلَوْلاَ تَذَكَّرُونَ} [الواقعة: 62], i.e. «فهلاَّ تَذَكَّرون» — so will you not remember, and know that He who originated something after it was not is able to restore it after its death and non-existence." End of quotation. So he made it an interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr), not of pure interrogation, and this is what it must be, because an interrogative does not come from the Exalted Creator except in this manner and the like.
The second view: that it has the meaning of «قد». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«هل» has the meaning of «قد» in interrogation specifically. The original is «أهل», by the evidence of the poet's words:
4430 - سائِلْ فوارسَ يَرْبوعٍ بشَدَّتِنا ... أهَلْ رَأَوْنا بوادي القُفِّ ذي الأَكَمِ
(Ask the horsemen of Yarbūʿ about our fierceness: have they seen us in the valley of al-Quff, with its hillocks?)
So the meaning is «أقد أتى», in the sense of both affirmation (taqrīr) and nearness (taqrīb), i.e. there came upon the human being, a short time before, a period of time in which he was not a thing mentioned, i.e. he was a thing forgotten, not mentioned." End of quotation. His phrase "in the sense of affirmation" means the meaning understood from the interrogative, which is what Makkī understood from «هل» itself; and his phrase "and nearness" means the meaning understood from «قد», in whose place «هل» has fallen. The meaning of his words "in interrogation specifically" is that «هل» is not used with the meaning of «قد» unless an interrogative accompanies it, either overtly, as in the preceding verse, or implicitly, as in the noble verse. So if you said «هل جاء زيدٌ» meaning «قد جاء» without an interrogative, it would not be permissible. Others have made it mean «قد» without this restriction. Some do not permit it at all, and interpret the verse of poetry as an instance of two particles of meaning being combined for emphasis, the difference in their wording making this acceptable, as in the poet's words:
4331 - فأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْأَلنْنَي عَنْ بِما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they came to be such that they no longer ask me about what is wrong with him...)
Here the «ب» has the meaning of «عن» and is emphasizing it. And if they have given emphasis even where the wording is identical, as in the poet's words:
4432 - فَلا واللَّهِ لا يُلْفَى لِما بي ... ولا لِلِما بهمْ أبداً دَواءُ
(No, by Allah, no remedy will ever be found for what afflicts me, nor for what afflicts them)
then they would all the more readily give emphasis where the wording differs. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing other than its having the meaning of «قد». There remained for al-Zamakhsharī one further restriction, namely that he should have said: "in verbal sentences", because whenever «هل» enters a nominal sentence it is impossible for it to have the meaning of «قد», since «قد» is specific to verbs. In my view this objection does not apply, because it is established that «قد» does not directly precede nouns.
His saying: {لَمْ يَكُن}: There are two views on this clause. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإِنسان», i.e. "Has there come upon him a period in this state?" The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «حينٌ», following another adjective. On this view the returning pronoun is implied: "a period in which he was not a thing mentioned". The first is the more apparent in both wording and meaning.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {أَمْشَاجٍ}: It is a naʿt (adjective) of «نُطْفة». The plural has occurred as a description of a singular because it is in the sense of a plural, as in His saying, the Exalted: {رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ}; or because each part of the sperm-drop was considered a sperm-drop, and so it was described with the plural. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أََمْشاج» is like «برمة أعشار» and «بُرْدٌ أكياش»; these are singular forms, not plurals, which is why they occur as descriptions of singulars." It is also said «نُطْفَةٌ مَشَجٌ». Al-Shammākh said:
4433 - طَوَتْ أَحْشاءَ مُرْتِجَةٍ لوَقْتٍ ... على مَشَجٍ سُلالتُه مَهِينُ
(She folded the insides of a [mare] closed for her time, upon a mixed [fluid] whose essence is base)
"And it is not valid for «أَمْشاج» to be a broken plural of it; rather the two are alike in being singular, since the singular is described by both." So he denied that «أمشاج» is the plural of «مِشْج» with kasra. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His statement contradicts the explicit statement of Sībawayh and the grammarians that «أفعال» cannot be a singular. Sībawayh said: 'There is no «أفعال» in the language except as a broken plural applied to a noun denoting a plurality; and whatever has occurred of a singular being described by «أفعال» they have interpreted.'" End of quotation. I say: he did not make «أفعال» a singular; he only said that the singular is described by it, meaning by the interpretation I have mentioned, namely that they treated each piece of the pot as a pot and each piece of the cloak as a cloak, and so described them with the plural. Al-Shaykh said: "«الأمْشاج» means mixtures; its singular is «مَشَج» (with two fathas), or «مِشْج» like «عِدْل» and «أعدال», or «مَشِيج» like «شريف» and «أشراف»; so said Ibn al-Aʿrābī. Ruʾba said:
4434 - يَطْرَحْن كلَّ مُعْجَلٍ نَشَّاجٍ ... لم يُكْسَ جِلْداً مِنْ دمٍ أَمْشاجِ
(They cast out every hasty [foetus], dripping, not yet clothed with skin, from mixed blood)
and the Hudhalī said:
4435 - كأن الرِّيْشَ والفُوْقَيْنِ منها ... خِلافَ النَّصْلِ سِيْطَ به مَشِيْجُ
(As if the feather and the two notches of it, beside the arrowhead, were mixed with a blend)
and al-Shammākh said:
4436 - طَوَتْ أحشاءَ مُرْتِجَةٍ. . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the verse [as above]. It is said «مَشَج يَمْشُجُ مَشْجاً» when one mixes, and «مَشيج» is like «خليط» and «مَمْشوج» like «مخلوط»." End of quotation. So he allowed it to be a plural of «مِشْج» like «عِدْل», though it has already been mentioned that al-Zamakhsharī denied that. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مَشَجَه» and «مَزَجَه» have the same meaning; the meaning is: from a sperm-drop in which the two fluids were mingled."
His saying: {نَّبْتَلِيهِ}: Two views are permissible for this clause. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «خَلَقْنا», i.e. "We created [him] while We were testing him". The second: that it is a ḥāl from «الإنسان»; this is valid because the clause contains two pronouns, each of which refers back to the possessor of the ḥāl. This ḥāl may then be concurrent if the meaning of «نَبْتَليه» is "We turn him about in his mother's womb as a sperm-drop, then a clot" — this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās — or it may be a prospective (muqaddara) ḥāl if the meaning of «نَبْتَليه» is "We test him with obligation", because at the time of his creation he is not under obligation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that what is meant is: transferring him from one state to another, which was called 'testing' by way of metaphor." I say: this is the meaning of Ibn ʿAbbās's saying mentioned above. Some said: "There is advancing and postponing in the sentence. The original is: «إنَّا جَعَلْناه سميعاً بصيراً نَبْتَليه», i.e. We made that for him for the sake of testing." But this is unnecessary.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِمَّا شَاكِراً}: «شاكراً» is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «هَدَيْناه», i.e. "We guided him, making clear to him both of his two states." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said that it is a prospective (muqaddara) ḥāl." I say: because he took the guidance to mean the initial making-clear to him, and at that time he is not characterised by either of the two attributes. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «السبيل», figuratively. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that both are ḥāls from «السبيل», i.e. We made the path known to him, either a grateful path or an ungrateful path, as in His saying: {وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النجدين} [البلد: 10]; so he described the path as gratitude and ingratitude figuratively."
The majority read «إمَّا» with kasra on the hamza, being synonymous with «أو»; the disagreement of the grammarians about it has been mentioned earlier. Makkī reported from the Kufans that here it is the conditional «إنْ» to which «ما» was added, and then said: "The Basrans do not permit this, because the conditional «إن» does not enter nouns unless a verb is implied, as in {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ} [التوبة: 6]. And implying the verb is not valid here, because that would require «شاكراً» to be nominative; moreover there is no evidence for the verb." End of quotation. I say: we do not concede that implying the verb requires «شاكراً» to be nominative; a verb that governs «شاكراً» in the accusative may be implied, its implied form being: "if We created him grateful, then he is very grateful; and if We created him ungrateful, then he is very ungrateful."
Abū l-Sammāl and Abū l-ʿAjjāj read it with fatḥa [on the hamza]. There are two views on it. The first: that it is the conjunctive [particle]; it is simply the dialect of some of them to give its hamza a fatḥa, and they recited in support of this:
4437 - يَلْفَحُها أمَّا شمالٌ عَرِيَّةٌ ... وأمَّا صَباً جِنْحَ العَشِيِّ هَبوبُ
(Either a cold north wind scorches it, or an easterly blowing at the edge of evening)
with fatḥa on the hamza. With the fatḥa on the hamza it is also permissible to replace its first mīm with yāʾ. He said:
4438 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أَيْما إلى جَنَّةٍ أَيْما إلى النارِ
(...either to a garden or to the Fire)
and he omitted the wāw between them. The second: that it is the «أمَّا» of detailing (tafṣīl), and its apodosis is implied. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a good reading, and the meaning is: as for the grateful, it is by Our granting of success; and as for the ungrateful, it is by his bad choice." End of quotation. He mentioned nothing else.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {سَلاَسِلَ}: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, Hishām and Abū Bakr read it with tanwīn, and the rest without tanwīn. These [with tanwīn] and Ḥamza and Qunbul stop on it with an alif without disagreement. Ibn Dhakwān, al-Bazzī and Ḥafṣ [stop] with the alif and without it, so the disagreement is reported from all three; and the rest stop without an alif without disagreement. So from this it emerges that the readers fall into [four] categories: those who add tanwīn in continuation and stop with the alif without disagreement, namely Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, Hishām and Abū Bakr; those who neither add tanwīn nor bring the alif in pausal form without disagreement, namely Ḥamza and Qunbul; those who do not add tanwīn and stop with the alif without disagreement, namely Abū ʿAmr alone; and those who do not add tanwīn and stop sometimes with the alif and sometimes without it, namely Ibn Dhakwān, Ḥafṣ and al-Bazzī. This is the utmost precision on the matter.
As for the tanwīn in «سلاسل», they have mentioned several explanations for it, among them: that he intended harmony, because what precedes it and what follows it is accusative with tanwīn. Among them: that al-Kisāʾī and others of the people of Kufa reported from some Arabs that they make all diptotes take tanwīn (ṣarf), except the «أفعل منك» form. Al-Akhfash said: "We heard from the Arabs some who give tanwīn to every diptote, because the original in nouns is to take tanwīn, and the withholding of it is for an incidental reason within them; and as for the plural, it can itself be pluralised, though rarely. They said «صواحب» and «صواحبات». In the ḥadīth: 'You are indeed the «صَواحِبات» of Yūsuf.' And the poet said:
4439 - قد جَرَتِ الطيرُ أيامِنينا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The birds have flown on our right-hand side...)
so he pluralised «أيامِن» with the sound masculine plural. And they recited: 4440 - وإذا الرجالُ رأوا يزيدَ رأيتَهمْ ... خُضُعَ الرِّقابِ نواكِسي الأبصارِ
(And when men see Yazīd, you see them with submissive necks, lowering their gazes)
with kasra on the sīn of «نواكِس», followed by a yāʾ that appears in writing but not in pronunciation because it dropped out through the meeting of two silent letters; the original is «نواكِسِين», where the nūn was dropped for the iḍāfa and the yāʾ for the meeting of two silent letters. This is according to the narration with kasra on the sīn; the more famous [narration] has fatḥa on the sīn, since when it was pluralised it came to resemble singular forms and so took tanwīn. Among them: that it is written with an alif in the codex of the Ḥijāz and of Kufa; Abū ʿUbayd narrated it, and Qālūn narrated it from Nāfiʿ. Some also narrated that from the codices of Basra." 
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "There are two views on it. The first: that this nūn is a substitute for the letter of release (ḥarf al-iṭlāq), and the continuation is treated like the pause. The second: that the person with this reading is one who was addicted to reciting poetry and whose tongue became accustomed to giving tanwīn to diptotes." I say: in this expression there is harshness and coarseness, especially towards the shaykhs of Islam and the leading, distinguished scholars.
These [readers] stopped with an overt alif. As for those who did not add tanwīn, it is evident, because it is of the form of the furthest plurals (muntahā l-jumūʿ). And their saying "it has been pluralised", as in «صَواحبات» and «أيامِنين», does no harm, because what is to be avoided is the broken plural, and this is a sound plural. The fact that they did not stop with the alif is also clear. As for those who did not add tanwīn and stopped with the alif, it is in following the noble orthography, as mentioned earlier; moreover the readers do not permit rawm [partial vowel] on a fatḥa, and the reader may wish to make the vowel clear in his pausal form, so they brought the alif so that the fatḥa would be made clear by it. It is reported from some that he says «رَأَيْتُ عُمَرا» with the alif, meaning ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. And «السَّلاسِلُ» is the plural of «سِلْسلة»; discussion of it has already been given.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {عَيْناً}: There are several views on its being accusative. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) for «كافوراً», because its water is like camphor in whiteness, scent and coolness. The second: that it is a badal for the position of «مِنْ كأسٍ»; so said Makkī, who did not imply an omitted muḍāf. Al-Zamakhsharī, on this view, implied an omitted muḍāf. He said: "It is as if it had been said: they drink wine, the wine of a spring." As for Abū l-Baqāʾ, he made the muḍāf implied on the view of its being a badal from «كافوراً», saying: "The second: it is a badal from «كافوراً», i.e. the water of a spring or the wine of a spring" — and this is a good meaning. The third: that it is the object of «يَشْرَبون», i.e. they drink a spring from a cup. The fourth: that it is accusative as specification of praise (ikhtiṣāṣ). The fifth: by implying «يَشْربون», which what follows explains; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ. There is some consideration in this, because the apparent sense is that what follows is a description of «عَيْن», so it is not valid for it to be an explanation. The sixth: by implying «يُعْطَوْن». The seventh: as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مِزاجُها»; so said Makkī.
«المِزاج» is that with which something is mixed, i.e. blended. It is said «مَزَجَه يَمْزُجه مَزْجاً», i.e. he blended it, «يَخلِطُه خَلْطاً». Ḥassān said: 4441 - كأنَّ سَبِيْئَةً مِنْ بيتِ رَأْسٍ ... يكونُ مِزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(As if a wine from Bayt Raʾs, whose mixture is honey and water)
So «المِزاج» is like «القِوام», a noun for that by which a thing is sustained. «والكافورُ» is a well-known perfume; its derivation is apparently from «الكَفْر», which is covering, because it covers things with its scent. Also «الكافور» is the sheaths of trees that cover their fruit. The object of «يَشْربون» is either omitted, i.e. they drink water or wine from a cup; or mentioned, and that is «عَيْناً» as stated above; or it is «مِنْ كأسٍ», with «مِنْ» redundant in it, and this proceeds on the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was the verb of drinking connected first with the particle of beginning and last with the particle of attachment? I say: because the cup is the starting point of their drinking and the first limit of it, whereas the spring is what they mix their drink with; so it is as if the meaning were: the servants of Allah drink the wine with it, as you say «شَرِبْتُ الماءَ بالعَسل» (I drank the water with honey)."
His saying: {يَشْرَبُ بِهَا}: There are several views on the «ب». The first: that it is redundant, i.e. «يَشْرَبُها», and the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla «يَشْرَبُها», transitive to the pronoun directly, indicates this. The second: that it has the meaning of «مِنْ». The third: that it is circumstantial, i.e. mixed with it. The fourth: that it is attached to «يَشْرَبُ», and the pronoun refers to the cup, i.e. they drink the spring by means of that cup, and the «ب» is for attachment, as mentioned earlier in al-Zamakhsharī's statement. The fifth: that it is on the basis of «يَشْرَبُون» implying the meaning: they take delight in it as drinkers. The sixth: on the basis of its implying the meaning of «يَرْوَى», i.e. the servants of Allah are quenched by it. Like this verse, in some of the views, is the saying of the Hudhalī:
4442 - شَرِبْنَ بماءِ البحرِ ثم تَرَفَّعَتْ ... متى لُجَجٍ خُضْرٍ لهنَّ نَئيجُ
(They drank of the sea water, then rose from green depths, with a roaring sound)
This allows for redundancy, and allows for its having the meaning of «مِنْ». The clause «يَشْرَبُ بها» is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of «عَيْناً», if we make the pronoun in «بها» refer to «عَيْناً» and do not make it an explanation of a governor, as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «قافوراً» with qāf in place of kāf; this is from the alternation between the two letters, as in their saying: «عربيٌّ قُحٌّ وكُحّ». And «يُفَجِّرونها» is in the position of ḥāl.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {يُوفُونَ}: It may be resumptive, having no position at all; and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an implied «كان». Al-Farrāʾ said: "The implied form is: «كانوا يُوْفُوْن بالنَّذْر في الدنيا، وكانوا يخَافون» (they used to fulfil their vows in the world, and they used to fear)." End of quotation. But this is unnecessary. The third: that it is an answer to someone who says: "Why are they given that provision?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: «يُوْفُوْن» is the answer to one who might say: "Why are they given that provision?" Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "He used «عَسَى» as the ṣila of «مَن», which is not permissible; and he brought the imperfect after «عَسَى» not accompanied by «أَنْ», which is rare or [found only] in poetry."
His saying: {كَانَ شَرُّهُ}: It is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of «يَومْ». «المُسْتَطِير» means the spread-out. It is said «استطار يَسْتطير اسْتِطارَةً فهو مُسْتَطير»; it is the form «استفعل» from «الطَّيران» (flying). The poet said: 4443 - فباتَتْ وقد أسْأَرَتْ في الفؤا ... دِصَدْعاً عل نَأْيِها مُسْتطيرا
(She spent the night having left in the heart a crack, spreading, upon her distance)
Al-Farrāʾ said: "«المُسْتطير» means «المُسْتطيل» (the long)." I say: it is as if he means that it is like it in meaning, not that he substituted a rāʾ for the lām. The dawn is of two kinds: the elongated, like the wolf's tail, which is the false [dawn], and the spreading, which is the true [dawn], because of its spreading across the horizon.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {حُبِّهِ}: It is a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from «الطعام», i.e. being [fed] in spite of their love for the food, or from the agent. The pronoun in «حُبِّه» refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. out of love for Allah. On either interpretation it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {قَمْطَرِيراً}: «القَمْطَرير» means severe. Its origin, as al-Zajjāj said, "is derived from «اقْمَطَرَّت الناقةُ», when the she-camel raises her tail, draws her flanks together and clamps her nose." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He derived it from «القَطْر» and made the mīm redundant." Asad b. Nāʿiṣa said:
4444 - واصْطَلَيْتُ الحروبُ في كلِّ يومٍ ... باسِلِ الشَّرِّ قَمْطَرِيرِ الصَّباحِ
(I have been scorched by wars every day, a day of fierce evil, grim in the morning)
Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The grammarians disagreed about this pattern; most do not accept the pattern «افْمَعَلَّ» among the verb patterns." It is said «اقْمَطَرَّ يَقْمَطِرُّ فهو مُقْمَطِرٌّ». The poet said:
4445 - تَلْزُبُ العقربُ تَزْبَئِرُّ ... تكسو استَها لحماً وتَقْمَطِرُّ
(The scorpion clings, bristling; it clothes its rear with flesh and curls up)
A day is «قَمْطرير» and «قُماطر», meaning severe. The poet said:
4446 - فَفِرُّوا إذا ما الحربُ ثارَ غبارُها ... ولَجَّ بها اليومُ الشديدُ القُماطِرُ
(So flee when war's dust has risen, and the grim, severe day has become fierce with it)
Al-Zajjāj said: "«القَمْطَرِيرْ» is that which frowns until what is between its eyes draws together." End of quotation. On this basis its use of a day is figurative. In some of al-Zamakhsharī's discussion he made it [derived] from «القَمْط», and on this basis the two rāʾs in it are redundant.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {بِمَا صَبَرُواْ}: «ما» is maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun). «جنةٌ» is a second object, i.e. He rewarded them with a garden for their patience. Makkī implied a muḍāf, saying: "Its implied form is: entering a garden and wearing silk."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {مُّتَّكِئِينَ}: It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «جَزاهم».
ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «وجازاهم». Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «مُتَّكئين» to be a ṣifa (adjective) of «جَنَّةً». But this is not permitted according to the Basrans, because the pronoun would have to be made overt, so that one would say «مُتَّكئين هم فيها», since the description is running on something other than what it belongs to. Makkī also denied that «مُتَّكئين» is a ṣifa of «جنةً», for the reason I mentioned, namely the non-appearance of the pronoun. Among those who held that «مُتَّكئين» is a ṣifa of «جَنَّةً» is al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "«مُتَّكئين», «لا يَرَوْن» and «دانيةً» may all be ṣifas of «جنةٌ»", but it is rejected by what I have mentioned. And it is not permissible for «مُتَّكئين» to be a ḥāl from the agent of «صَبَروا», because the patience was in the world and their reclining is only in the Hereafter; Makkī said the like. Someone may say: if the only obstacle is this, then make it a prospective (muqaddara) ḥāl, because their destination, on account of their patience, is this state. There are parallels for it.
And His saying: {إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ} is either on the implying of "saying", i.e. saying that. Abū Jaʿfar read «فَوَقَّاهم» with shadda on the qāf, for intensification.
His saying: {لاَ يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا}: There are several views on it. The first: that it is a second ḥāl from the object of «جزاهم». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the latent nominative pronoun in «مُتَّكئين», making it a nested ḥāl. The third: that it is a ṣifa of «جنة», like «متكئين», according to those who hold that, and it has already been mentioned that it is al-Zamakhsharī's view.
«والزَّمْهَرير» is the most intense cold. This is the well-known [meaning]. Thaʿlab said: it is the moon in the language of Ṭayyiʾ, and he recited:
4447 - في ليلةٍ ظلامُها قد اعتكَرْ ... قَطَعْتُها والزَّمْهريرُ ما زَهَرْ
(In a night whose darkness had grown dense, I crossed it while the moon had not shone)
The meaning is that the Garden has no need of sun or moon. Its pattern is «فَعْلَلِيل».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَدَانِيَةً}: The majority read it in the accusative, and there are several views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to the position of «لا يَرَوْن». The second: that it is conjoined to «مُتَّكئين», so it carries what that carries. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «ودانيةً عليهم ظلالُها» — to what is it conjoined? I say: to the clause before it, because it is in the position of ḥāl from those rewarded, and this is a ḥāl like it about them, because the pronoun in «عليهم» refers back to them; except that it is a singular noun, whereas that is a group in the status of a singular. Its implied form is: not seeing in it sun or intense cold, and [seeing the shade] near. The wāw entered to indicate that the two matters are combined for them. It is as if it had been said: He rewarded them with a garden, combining in it freedom from heat and cold and the nearness of shade over them." The third: that it is a ṣifa of an omitted noun, i.e. «وجنةً دانِيَةً»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ. The fourth: that it is a ṣifa of the expressed «جنة»; so said al-Zajjāj.
Abū Ḥaywa read «ودانِيَةٌ» in the nominative. There are two views on it. The more apparent: that «ظلالُها» is a mubtadaʾ and «دانيةٌ» a fronted khabar, the clause being in the position of ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: they see in it neither sun nor intense cold, while its shades are near over them." The second: that «دانيةٌ» is nominative by ibtidāʾ and «ظلالُها» is the agent of it; al-Akhfash used it as evidence for the permissibility of the active participle's governing even when it does not rely on anything, as in «قائمٌ الزيدون», for «دانية» does not rely on anything of what the grammarians mention, yet «ظلالُها» has been put in the nominative by it. But there is no proof for him in this, since it may be a mubtadaʾ with a fronted khabar, as mentioned.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also reported with the genitive, i.e. «في جنَّةٍ دانية». That is weak, because it would be conjoined to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition." I say: he means that «ودانِيَةٍ» was read irregularly in the genitive, as a ṣifa of an omitted noun, and it would then be a conjunction upon the genitive pronoun in His saying «لا يَرَوْنَ فيها», i.e. "and not in a near garden". This is the opinion of the Kufans, who permit conjunction upon the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition; and for that reason he considered it weak. Discussion of this has already been given at length in al-Baqara.
As for the nominative «ظلالُها», it may be a mubtadaʾ with «عليهم» as fronted khabar, and it is not nominative by «دانية», because «دنا» is made transitive by «إلى», not by «على». The second: that it is nominative by «دانية», on the basis that it implies the meaning of «مُشْرِفَة» (overlooking), because «دنا» and «أَشْرَفَ» are close in meaning; Abū l-Baqāʾ said the like. These two views also apply to the reading of those who put «دانيةً» in the accusative.
Al-Aʿmash read «ودانِياً» in the masculine, because of the separation between the adjective and its nominative by «عليهم», or because the plural is treated as masculine.
Ubayy read «ودانٍ عليهم» in the masculine, nominative; it is a witness for al-Akhfash's view, since he puts [the following noun] in the nominative by the active participle even though it does not rely on anything. And it cannot be parsed as mubtadaʾ with fronted khabar for lack of agreement. Makkī said: "«دانِياً» was read," then said: "«ودانيةٌ» in the nominative is permissible, and «دانٍ» in the nominative and masculine is permissible", without stating explicitly that the two were [actually] read; yet it has already been mentioned that they are read, so it seems he was not aware of that.
His saying: {وَذُلِّلَتْ}: It may be in the position of the accusative as ḥāl, conjoined to «دانِيَةً» for those who put it in the accusative, i.e. «ومُذَلَّلةً». It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عليهم», whether you put «دانِيَةً» in the accusative, the nominative, or the genitive. It may also be resumptive. As for the reading with «ودانيةٌ» in the nominative, it would be a verbal sentence conjoined to a nominal one; and it may be a ḥāl, as mentioned.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {بِآنِيَةٍ}: This is what stands in the place of the agent, because it is the direct object in meaning. «عليهم» is also possible. «وآنِيَة» is the plural of «إناء»; the original is «أَأْنِيَة» with two hamzas, the first redundant for the plural and the second the fāʾ of the word, so the second is turned into an alif necessarily. This is like «كِساءٌ» and «أَكْسِيَة», «وغِطاءٌ» and «أَغْطِيَة»; and its parallel in a sound-lām word is «حِمار» and «أَحْمِرة». And «مِنْ فضةٍ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آنية».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {قَوَارِيرَاْ قَوَارِيرَاْ}: The readers disagreed on these two words with regard to tanwīn and its absence, and to stopping with the alif and without it, as their disagreement was mentioned earlier regarding {سَلاَسِلَ}. Know that the readers on the two fall into five categories. The first: tanwīn on both, and stopping on both with the alif, for Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr. The second: the opposite of this, namely no tanwīn on either and no stopping on either with the alif, for Ḥamza alone. The third: no tanwīn on either, and stopping on both with the alif, for Hishām alone. The fourth: tanwīn on the first but not the second, and stopping on the first with the alif and on the second without it, for Ibn Kathīr alone. The fifth: no tanwīn on either, and stopping on the first with the alif and on the second without it, for Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Dhakwān and Ḥafṣ.
As for those who gave tanwīn to both, it is for the reason given under the tanwīn of «سلاسل», because they are of the form of the furthest plurals: that one on «مَفاعِل», this on «مَفاعيل». The stopping is with the alif that is a substitute for the tanwīn, and in it is agreement with the codices mentioned, for the two are written in them with the alif, as Abū ʿUbayd reported. The absence of tanwīn and of stopping with the alif is entirely clear. As for him who gave tanwīn to the first but not the second, he harmonised the first with the verse-endings, and did not harmonise the second with the first. The reason for his stopping on the first with the alif and on the second without it is clear. Abū ʿUbayd reported that it is so in the codices of the people of Basra.
As for him who gave no tanwīn to either, and stopped on the first with the alif and on the second without it: it is because the first is a verse-end, so he harmonised it with the verse-ends by stopping with the alif, and distinguished it from the second because it is not a verse-end. As for him who gave no tanwīn to either and stopped on both with the alif: he harmonised the first with the verse-ends and harmonised the second with the first. From what preceded regarding «سلاسل» and these two words it emerges that among the readers some agreed with their codex and some differed from it in following the transmitted report. Discussion of «قوارير» has been given in Sūrat al-Naml, and praise be to Allah.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This tanwīn is a substitute for the letter of release (ḥarf al-iṭlāq), because it is a verse-final; and in the second it is to follow the first." He means that they bring tanwīn as a substitute for the letter of release that is for chanting, as in the saying:
4448 - يا صاحِ ما هاجَ الدُّموعَ الذُّرَّفَنْ ...
(O friend, what has stirred the streaming tears?)
There are two views on the accusative of «قوارير». The first, which is the apparent one: that it is the khabar of «كان». The second: that it is a ḥāl, and «كان» is complete, i.e. "they were brought into being and so they were." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The repetition is good because of the explanation of their origin which is attached to it; and without the repetition it would not be good for the first to be a verse-end, because of the strong attachment of the adjective to the described." Al-Aʿmash read «قواريرُ» in the nominative, on the implying of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. they are «قوارير». And «مِنْ فضة» is a ṣifa of «قوارير».
His saying: {قَدَّرُوهَا}: It is a ṣifa of «قواريرَ». There are two views on the wāw in «قَدَّروها». The first: that it is for those who are served. The meaning of their measuring it is that they measured it in their own minds to be of measures and shapes according to their desires, and it came as they measured.
The second: that the wāw is for those who go around, as indicated by His saying «ويُطافُ»; the meaning is that they measured its drink according to the quenching of the drinker, which is the most delightful drink since it is according to the measure of his need, neither exceeding it nor falling short; so said al-Zamakhsharī. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed the clause to be resumptive.
ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Sulamī, al-Shaʿbī, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Abū ʿAmr in al-Aṣmaʿī's narration read «قُدِّرُوْها» in the passive. Al-Fārisī made it a case of inversion (maqlūb). He said: "It is as if the wording were «قُدِّروا عليها». In the meaning there is inversion, because the truth of the meaning is that one should say «قُدِّرَتْ عليهم»; so it is like His saying: {لَتَنُوءُ بالعصبة أُوْلِي القوة} [القصص: 76], and like the saying of the Arabs: «إذا طَلَعَتِ الجَوْزاءُ أُلْقِيَ العُوْدُ على الحِرْباء»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its explanation is that it is from «قُدِّر», transferred from «قَدَر». You say «قَدَرْتُ [الشيءَ]» and «قَدَرَنيه فلان» when he made you able to do it; its meaning is: they were made able over them [the vessels] as they wished, and they were given free rein to measure according to what they desired." Abū Ḥātim said: "The vessels were measured according to the extent of their quenching." Some explained this statement of Abū Ḥātim, saying: "There is omission upon omission in it: the original was «قُدِّرَ على قَدْرِ ريِّهم إياها»; then «على» was omitted and it became «قَدْرُ رِيِّهم» as the passive subject; then «قَدْرُ» was omitted and it became «رِيُّهم» as the passive subject; then «الرِّيُّ» was omitted and the wāw took the place of the hāʾ and mīm when the muḍāf before them was omitted, and the wāw became the passive subject, and the pronoun of the second object, in the position of the accusative, attached to the verb after the wāw that had been turned from the hāʾ and mīm, until they were made to stand in the place of the agent." I say: in this derivation there is an affectation that is not hidden, along with the harshness of its wording.
Al-Shaykh said: "The nearest explanation of this irregular reading is: «قُدِّرَ رِيُّهم منها تقديراً»; the muḍāf, which is «الرِّيُّ», was omitted and the pronoun put in its place, so the implied form became «قُدِّروا مِنْها»; then latitude was applied to the verb, «مِنْ» was omitted and the verb reached the pronoun directly, so it became «قُدِّرُوْها». So there is in it nothing but the omission of a muḍāf and latitude in the verb." I say: this is drawn from the explanation of Abū Ḥātim's statement.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {زَنجَبِيلاً}: «الزَّنجبيل» is a well-known plant, and the cup is so named because the taste of ginger is found in it. The Arabs find it delightful. Al-Zamakhsharī recited from al-Aʿshā: 4449 - كأنَّ القُرُنْفُلَ والزَّنْجَبِيْ ... لَ باتا بفِيْها وأَرْياً مَشُورا
(As if cloves and ginger had spent the night in her mouth, together with gathered honey)
and he recited from al-Musayyab b. ʿAlas:
4450 - وكأن طَعْمَ الزَّنْجبيلِ به ... إذا ذُقْتَه وسُلافةَ الخمرِ
(As if the taste of ginger were in it, when you tasted it, and the choicest of wine)
And «عَيْناً» here has the views mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {سَلْسَبِيلاً}: «السَّلْسَبيل» is what flows down easily in the throat. Al-Zajjāj said: "In the language it is a description of what is in the utmost smoothness." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is said: a drink is «سَلْسَلٌ», «سَلْسالٌ» and «سَلْسبيل»; the bāʾ was added in the composition until the word became quinqueliteral, and it indicates the utmost smoothness." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If he meant that it was truly added, that is not good, because the bāʾ is not among the letters of addition known in the science of grammar; if he meant that it is a letter that came in the root of the word, and is not in «سَلْسَل» or «سَلْسال», then it is correct, and it would be among what agrees in meaning but differs in material." Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "I have not heard «السَّلْسبيل» except in the Qurʾān." Makkī said: "It is a non-Arabic indefinite noun, and for that reason it takes tanwīn."
The pattern of «سَلْسَبيل» is «فَعْلَلِيْل», like «دَرْدَبيس». It was also said: «فَعْفَليل», because the fāʾ is repeated. Ṭalḥa read «سَلْسَبيلَ» without tanwīn; it is withheld from tanwīn [as a diptote] for being a proper name and feminine, because it is the name of one particular spring. On this basis, how was it given tanwīn in the reading of the majority? The answer: it was so named not as a proper name but as a bare designation; or it is a case of the tanwīn of {سَلاَسِلَ} [الإِنسان: 4] and {قَوَارِيرَاْ} [الإِنسان: 15], which has been mentioned. The strangest thing said about this word is that it is composed of two words: an imperative verb, a latent agent and an object; the implied form being: «سَلْ أنت سَبيلا إليها» (ask for a way to it). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They attributed to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that its meaning is «سَلْ سبيلاً إليها». This is not sound on its face, unless it is meant that the whole sentence of the speaker's «سَلْ سبيلاً» was made a proper name for the spring, as was said of «تأبَّط شَرَّاً» and «ذَرَّى حبَّا». It was so named because no one drinks from it except one who asks for a way to it through righteous deeds. Despite its soundness in Arabic, it is an affectation and an innovation, and attributing it to someone like ʿAlī, peace be upon him, is more innovative still." In the poetry of some of the moderns:
4451 - سَلْ سبيلاً فيها إلى راحةِ النَّفْ ... سِ براحٍ كأنَّها سَلْسَبيلُ
(Ask for a way in it to the ease of the soul, with wine as if it were salsabīl)
Al-Shaykh said after expressing his astonishment at this saying: "More astonishing than that is al-Zamakhsharī's giving it a direction and busying himself with relating it." I say: had he considered what al-Zamakhsharī said, he would not have blamed him nor been astonished at him, because al-Zamakhsharī is the one who denounced this saying in the strongest terms. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«السلسبيل» is a single word." In his saying "a single word" is a hint and allusion to the view mentioned.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {ثَمَّ}: This is an adverb of place, specific to distance. There are two views on its being accusative here, the more apparent being that it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). The object of seeing is not mentioned, because the intent is: "and when a seeing proceeds from you in that place, you see such-and-such"; so the second «رَأَيْتَ» is the apodosis of «إذا». Al-Farrāʾ said: «ثَمَّ» is the direct object of «رَأَيْتَ». Al-Farrāʾ also said: "«وإذا رَأَيْتَ» has the implied form «ما ثَمَّ», so «ما» is the object; «ما» was omitted and «ثَمَّ» stands in the place of «ما»." Al-Zamakhsharī, following Abū Isḥāq, said: "Whoever says its meaning is «ما ثَمَّ» has erred, because «ثَمَّ» is the ṣila of «ما», and it is not permissible to drop the relative noun and leave the ṣila." There is something to consider in this, because the Kufans permit the like of this and cited verses of poetry and Qurʾānic verses as evidence, discussed in full at the beginning of this work.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«وثَمَّ» is an adverbial; its governor is «رَأَيْتَ» or its meaning, the implied form being: you saw what is there, «ما» having been omitted." Al-Shaykh said: "This is invalid, because insofar as he makes it governed by «رَأَيْتَ» it cannot be the ṣila of «ما», since its governor in that case is omitted, i.e. 'what is settled there'." I say: it can be answered that his saying "or its meaning" is the statement that it is a ṣila of a relative noun, so there are two views, not one view, such that invalidity would follow; were it not so, his saying "or its meaning" would have no sense. By "its meaning" he means the meaning of the verb in terms of the sentence, namely the implied "settling".
The majority read the thāʾ of «ثَمَّ» with fatḥa, as mentioned. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it with ḍamma, as the conjunctive [«ثُمَّ»], conjoining the second «رأَيْتَ» to the first; the verb of the apodosis is then omitted, and this omitted verb of the apodosis is the governor of the accusative in His saying «نعيماً»; the implied form is: "and when a seeing proceeds from you, then another seeing proceeds, you will see bliss and a kingdom." So this «رَأَيْتَ» is the apodosis.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {عَالِيَهُمْ}: Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza read it with sukūn on the yāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the hāʾ. When the yāʾ is silent the hāʾ takes kasra, and when it is vowelled it takes ḍamma, as established regarding the pronoun hāʾ at the beginning of this work. As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza, there are several views on it, the most apparent being that it is a fronted khabar, and «ثيابُ» a postponed mubtadaʾ. The second: that «عالِيْهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «ثيابُ» is nominative as its agent, even though the adjective does not rely on anything; this is al-Akhfash's view.
The third: that «عالِيْهم» is accusative and was made silent for lightness; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ. If it is accusative, several views apply to it, and they apply here; except that implying the fatḥa on a defective noun is not permissible except in necessity or anomaly, and this reading is mutawātir (broadly transmitted), so it ought not to be said of it.
As for the reading of those who put it in the accusative, there are several views. The first: that it is an adverbial, a fronted khabar, and «ثيابُ» a postponed mubtadaʾ, as if it were said: "above them are garments." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because «عالِيَهم» means «فَوْقَهم»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In the accusative it may be adverbial because it has the meaning of «فوقهم»." Al-Shaykh said: "«عالٍ» and «عالية» are active participles, so to [establish] their being adverbials it must be transmitted from the speech of the Arabs: «عالِيَك أو عاليتُك ثوبُ»." I say: words of the form of active participles have occurred as adverbials, such as «خارجَ الدار» and «داخلَها» and «باطنَها» and «ظاهرَها». You say «جلَسْتُ خارج الدارِ», and likewise the rest, so this is likewise.
The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in {عَلَيْهِمْ} [الإِنسان: 19]. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the object of {حَسِبْتَهُمْ} [الإِنسان: 19]. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from an implied muḍāf, i.e. "you saw people of bliss and a great kingdom, with garments above them", so «عاليَهم» is a ḥāl from the implied «أهل». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these three views, saying: "«وعاليَهم» in the accusative is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَطوف عليهم» or in «حَسِبْتَهم», i.e. «يطوفُ عليهم وِلْدانٌ عالياً للمَطوفِ عليهم ثيابٌ», or «حَسِبْتَهم لؤلؤاً عاليَهم ثيابٌ». It may also be meant: [you saw] people of bliss." Al-Shaykh said: "As for its being a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حَسِبْتَهم», he can only mean the object pronoun, which returns only to «وِلدانٌ»; therefore he implied «عاليَهم» as «عالياً لهم», i.e. for the boys. This is not suitable, because the pronouns that come afterwards indicate that they are for those served, from His saying «وحُلُّوا» and «سَقاهم» and {إِنَّ هذا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَآءً}; and untying the pronouns and making this for one and that for another, without need or compulsion for it, is not permissible. As for making it a ḥāl from an omitted noun with the implied form «أهلَ نعيم», there is no need to claim omission when the speech is sound and excellent without implying that omission."
I say: making one of the pronouns for one thing and another for something else does not prevent the soundness of that, given what distinguishes the return of each to what suits it; likewise implying an omission is not forbidden either, though it is better that the pronouns agree and that no omission be implied. Al-Zamakhsharī only mentioned that by way of permissibility, not as being preferable or equal, so it should not be refuted by what he has mentioned.
The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «لَقَّاهم». The sixth: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «جَزاهُمْ»; Makkī mentioned both. On these views in which it is accusative as ḥāl, «ثيابُ» is nominative by it as agent, and its being annexed to a definite noun does not harm its occurring as ḥāl, because the annexation is verbal (lafẓiyya), as in His saying, the Exalted: {عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [الأحقاف: 24] [and the saying:]
4452 - يا رُبَّ غابِطِنا. . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O many a one who envies us...)
«عالياً» was not made feminine because its nominative is not truly feminine. The seventh: that «عاليَهم» is accusative as an adverbial, and «ثيابُ» is nominative by it as agent. This proceeds on the view of al-Akhfash and the Kufans, who make the adverbial and its equivalent govern even when it does not rely on anything, as mentioned regarding the adjective. When «عاليَهم» is nominative by ibtidāʾ and «ثيابُ» is its agent, it is a singular in its normal sense because it stands in the place of the verb; and when it is made a fronted khabar it is a singular intended as a plural, so it is like His saying, the Exalted: {فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ القوم} [الأنعام: 45], i.e. «أدبار»; so said Makkī.
Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd b. ʿAlī read «عاليتُهم» feminine with tā', nominative. Al-Aʿmash and Abān, from ʿĀṣim, [read] likewise, except that it is accusative; you know the nominative and accusative from what preceded, so there is no need to repeat them. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, read «عَلِيَتْهم» as a past verb attached to the silent tāʾ of the feminine, with «ثيابُ» its agent; it strengthens the views mentioned for the nominative of «ثياب» by the adjective in the reading of the rest, as detailed earlier.
Ibn Sīrīn, Mujāhid, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and many others read «عليهم» as preposition and its genitive noun; its parsing is like the parsing of «عاليَهم» as an adverbial, in that it may be a fronted khabar or a ḥāl as mentioned before, and «ثيابُ» is nominative by it, according to the detail given just above.
The majority read «ثيابُ سُنْدُسٍ» with the annexation of «ثياب» to what follows. Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read] «ثيابٌ» with tanwīn, «سُندُسٌ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ» all in the nominative; so «سندسٌ» is a naʿt of «ثيابٌ», because «السُّنْدس» is a kind, and «خُضْرٌ» is a naʿt of «سندس», since sundus may be green or not green, just as garments may be of sundus or other than it. And «إستبرقٌ» is a conjunction on what precedes it, i.e. «وثياب استبرق».
Know that the seven readers on «خُضْر وإستبرق» fall into four categories. The first: nominative on both, for Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ only. The second: genitive on both, for the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] only. The third: nominative on the first and genitive on the second, for Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir only. The fourth: the reverse of the third, for Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr only. As for the first reading: the nominative of «خُضْرٌ» is as naʿt of «ثياب», and the nominative of «إستبرقٌ» is as conjunction on «الثياب», but with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «وثيابُ إستبرقٍ». Likewise: «على زيدٍ ثوبُ خَزٍّ وكتَّانٌ», i.e. «وثوبُ كُتَّانٍ». As for the second reading, the genitive of «خُضْرٍ» is as naʿt of «سُنْدسٍ». It was then found problematic that a singular be described by a plural, so Makkī said: "It is a noun of collection. It was also said that it is the plural of «سُنْدُسَة», like «تَمْر» and «تَمْرة», and a generic noun may be described with a plural, soundly and eloquently. The Exalted said: {وَيُنْشِىءُ السحاب الثقال} [الرعد: 12]. And since they have described a singular with the definite article, because the genus is meant by it, with a plural, in their saying «أَهْلَكَ الناسَ الدِّينارُ الحُمْرُ والدِّرْهَمُ البيضُ», and in the Revelation {أَوِ الطفل الذين} [النور: 31], then to find that in nouns of collection or generic nouns, which are distinguished from their singular by the tāʾ of the feminine, is all the more fitting." The genitive of «إستبرق» is as conjunction on «سندسٍ», because the meaning is: garments of sundus and garments of istabraq.
As for the third reading: the nominative of «خُضْرٌ» is as naʿt of «ثيابٌ» and the genitive of «إستبرقٍ» is as conjunction on «سُنْدُسٍ», i.e. green garments of sundus and of istabraq; on this basis istabraq is also green.
As for the fourth reading: the genitive of «خُضْرٍ» is as naʿt of «سُنْدس», and the nominative of «إستبرقٌ» is as conjunction on «ثياب» with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «وثيابُ إستبرق». Discussion of the root of «السُّنْدُس» and «الإِستبرق» and what was said of them has already been given in Sūrat al-Kahf.
Ibn Muḥayṣin read «وإستبرقَ» with fatḥa on the qāf. The transmission from him is then inconsistent about the hamza: some report from him that he made it a hamzat qaṭʿ, and some report from him that he made it a hamzat waṣl.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وإسْتبرقَ» was read in the accusative in the position of the genitive, as a diptote because it is non-Arabic; and this is a mistake, because it is an indefinite noun which the definite article enters; you say «الإِستبرق» — unless Ibn Muḥayṣin claims that it is made a proper name for this type of garment. «واستبرقَ» was also read with hamzat waṣl and fatḥa, on the basis that it is named with the form «اسْتَفْعل» from «البريق» (gleaming); that is not correct either, because it is an Arabicised word whose Arabicisation is well known, and its origin is «اسْتَبْرَه»." Al-Shaykh said: "His saying «unless Ibn Muḥayṣin claims» and his saying afterwards «and «واستبرق» was read with hamzat waṣl and fatḥa» indicate that Ibn Muḥayṣin's reading is with hamzat qaṭʿ and fatḥa on the qāf. But what is transmitted from him in the books of qirāʾāt is that he read with hamzat waṣl and fatḥa on the qāf." I say: Makkī preceded al-Zamakhsharī in this, for he said: "Ibn Muḥayṣin read it as a diptote, and it is a mistake if he made it a noun, because it is an indefinite triptote. It was also said that he made it a past verb from «بَرِقَ», which is permissible in wording but far-fetched in meaning.
It was also said: it is originally a past verb on «اسْتَفْعل» from «بَرِقَ», so it is Arabic, from «البريق»; when it was used as a name its alif was made a qaṭʿ, because it is not of the nature of nouns that the alif of waṣl enter them; it has entered only some defective nouns that were altered from their origin, which are limited and cannot be used as a basis for analogy." End of quotation. His saying «its alif was made a qaṭʿ» to the end indicates that he read with hamzat qaṭʿ and fatḥa on the qāf. And his saying earlier «It was also said that he made it a past verb from «بَرِقَ»» indicates that he read with hamzat waṣl, because it cannot be imagined that it be judged a verb, not transferred to nouns, with its alif left as a hamzat qaṭʿ at all, for this would be ignorance of the language; so two readings are reported from him, the qaṭʿ of the alif and its waṣl. It is thus evident that al-Zamakhsharī was not alone in reporting the qaṭʿ of the hamza from Ibn Muḥayṣin.
Abū Ḥātim said regarding the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin: "It is not permissible. The correct view is that it is a generic noun which should not carry a pronoun, and entry of the definite article upon it supports that. The correct course is the qaṭʿ of the alif and treating it according to the reading of the majority." Al-Shaykh said: "We say: Ibn Muḥayṣin is an eminent reader well known for his knowledge of Arabic, and he took from the greatest scholars, so a direction must be sought for his reading, and that is that he makes it [the form] «استفعل» from «البريق»; you say «بَرِقَ» and «اسْتَبْرَق», like «عَجِبَ» and «استعجب». And since His saying «خُضْر» indicates greenness, which is the colour of that sundus, and greenness, owing to its intensity, may contain darkness and dullness, He informed that in it there is a gleam and beauty that removes its dullness; so «استبرق» is a past verb, and the pronoun in it refers to the sundus, or to the green indicated by «خُضْر». This explanation is preferable to declaring ungrammatical someone who knows Arabic, and to declaring a reliable, precise [transmitter] mistaken." I say: this is what Makkī mentioned as I have related from him; this reading was already discussed in Sūrat al-Kahf, and I only repeated it for the sake of this additional benefit.
His saying: {وحلوا}: It is conjoined to «ويَطوف»; it conjoins a verb past in wording and future in meaning, and presents it in the past form for the certainty of its occurrence. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after a question and answer concerning meaning: "How fine it is for the wrist to bear two bracelets: a bracelet of gold and a bracelet of silver!" Al-Shaykh took him to task over his saying «بالمِعْصم», saying: "His saying «بالمِعْصم» is either the object of «أَحْسن» with «أَنْ يكونَ» as a substitute from it, or «أنْ يكونَ» is the object of «أَحْسن» with the preposition and its genitive noun separating them. If it is the first, it is not permissible, because the addition of the bāʾ in the object of the verb of wonder in the «أَفْعَلَ» form is unknown; you do not say «ما أحسنَ بزيدٍ» meaning «ما أحسن زيداً». If it is the second, there is disagreement about such separation, and what is transmitted from some is that it is not permissible, and a later-born speaker like ourselves, when he speaks, ought to guard in his speech against what is disputed." I say: what purpose has he in pursuing the speech of this man, even in this trivial matter? Though the correct view is that it is permissible, and it is what is heard from the Arabs in prose. ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib said: «للَّهِ دَرُّ بني فلانٍ ما أشَدَّ في الهيجاءِ لقاءَها، وأَثْبَتَ في المَكْرُمات بقاءَها، وأحسنَ في اللَّزَبات عطاءَها» (How excellent are the sons of so-and-so! How fierce in battle is their meeting, how firm in noble deeds their endurance, how fine in hard times their giving!). Occupying oneself with something other than this is more fitting.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا}: «نحن» may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «إنَّ», or it may be a separating pronoun (faṣl); on these two aspects «نَزَّلْنا» is the khabar of «إنَّ». And «نحن» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «نَزَّلْنا» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». Makkī said: «"نحنُ" is in the position of an accusative as an attribute of the noun of "إنَّ", because a pronoun is described by a pronoun, since it is in the sense of emphasis, not in the sense of characterisation (taḥliya); and it is not described by an overt noun, because that is in the sense of characterisation, while the pronoun has no need of characterisation, since it is only used as a pronoun after its characterisation and identity are known; so it needs emphasis to confirm the predication about it.» I say: this is a very strange expression. How can a pronoun be made to be described by its like? We know of no disagreement about the impermissibility of describing a pronoun, except what is transmitted from al-Kisāʾī, that he permitted describing the third-person pronoun with an overt noun — you say «مَرَرْتُ به العاقل» ("I passed by him, the intelligent one"), with «العاقل» as a naʿt (adjective). As for describing a pronoun other than the third person with another pronoun, there is no disagreement about its impermissibility. Moreover, his words come down to emphasis, so there is no need to depart from it.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {أَوْ كَفُوراً}: regarding this «أو» there are several aspects. The first: it is in its proper sense; this is the view of Sībawayh. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «In prohibition it conveys [the prohibition] of all, because when you say in permission "Sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn", the implied meaning is: sit with one of them. So when one prohibits and says "Do not speak to Zayd or ʿAmr", the implied meaning is: do not speak to one of them; so whichever of them he speaks to is one of them, and he is prohibited from it. Likewise in the verse, and the meaning comes down to: do not obey of them either a sinner or an ungrateful one.» al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: the meaning of "أو" is "do not obey one of them"; why was the wāw not brought, so that it would be a prohibition of obeying both of them together? I say: if it were said "do not obey both of them", it would be permissible for him to obey one of them. When it is said "do not obey one of them", it is known that he who prohibits obeying one of them prohibits all the more strongly obeying both of them together, just as when one is prohibited from saying "uff" to his parents, it is known that he is prohibited from striking them a fortiori.» The second: it is in the sense of «لا», i.e. do not obey one who sinned nor one who disbelieved. Makkī said: «This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it is in the sense of the permission that we mentioned.» The third: it is in the sense of the wāw; it has preceded that this is the view of the Kufans, and their proofs have preceded.
And «الكفور», even though it entails sin, was conjoined for one of two reasons: either they are two particular persons — in the tafsīr: the sinner is ʿUtba and the ungrateful one is al-Walīd — or for what al-Zamakhsharī said. He said: «If you say: they were all disbelievers, so what is the meaning of the division in His saying "a sinner or an ungrateful one"? I say: its meaning is: do not obey of them one committing what is a sin, calling you to it, or one doing what is disbelief, calling you to it; because they either called him to assist them in an act that is sin or disbelief, or one that is neither sin nor disbelief; so he was prohibited from assisting them in the two, not the third.»

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {وَسَبِّحْهُ}: in it is a proof against what some scholars of maʿānī and bayān said, that combining ḥāʾ and hāʾ, for example, takes the word out of its eloquence; they counted among this the poet's saying:
4453 - كريمٌ متى أَمْدَحْه أَمْدَحْه والوَرَى ... معي وإذا ما لُمْتُه لُمْتُه وَحْدي
(A noble man: whenever I praise him, I praise him with all mankind with me; and when I blame him, I blame him alone.)
The verse is by Abū Tammām. It is possible to distinguish between what they recited and the noble verse, in that what takes the verse out of eloquence is the repetition, unlike the noble verse, in which there is no repetition.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {يَوْماً}: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يَذَرُون», not an adverb (ẓarf). Its description with heaviness is figurative, because [heaviness] is among the attributes of concrete things, not of abstract ones. «وراء» here is in the sense of "in front of" (quddām). Makkī said: «It was called "warāʾ" because it is hidden (tawārī) from you»; the apparent sense of this is that it is literal, whereas the correct view is that it was borrowed for "in front of". It was also said: rather, it is in its proper sense, i.e. behind their backs, paying no heed to it; and in it there is a figurative extension.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا شِئْنَا}: al-Zamakhsharī said: «Properly it should come with "إنْ", not with "إذا", as in His saying: {وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْاْ يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ} [Muḥammad: 38], {إِن يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 133].» He means that «إذا» is for what is certain and «إنْ» for what is possible, and He, Exalted is He, did not will that. The answer to it is that «إذا» may occur in the place of «إنْ», just as the reverse.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله}: there are two aspects to it. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. except in the state of Allah's willing; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It is questionable, because this is rendered as a definite [noun], unless he means explaining the meaning. The second: it is an adverb (ẓarf). al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the position of {أَن يَشَآءَ الله}? I say: accusative as an adverb; its origin is: except at the time of Allah's willing. Likewise Ibn Masʿūd read "إِلاَّ مَا يشَآءُ الله", because "ما" with the verb is like "أَنْ".» The Shaykh rejected it, [saying] that nothing stands in the place of an adverb except the explicit maṣdar (verbal noun): «If you said "I will come to you that the cock crows" or "what the cock crows", it would not be permissible.» I say: the discussion with him about this has preceded more than once.
Nāfiʿ and the Kufans read «تَشاؤُون», in address to all creatures, or by way of iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person in His saying: «نحن خَلَقْناهم». The rest [read it] in the third person, in keeping with His saying «خَلَقْناهم» and what follows it.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ}: accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by a verb explained by «أعدَّ لهم» in meaning, not in wording, its implied form being: and He punished the wrongdoers; similar to it is «زيداً مَرَرْتُ به», i.e. I passed and came into contact [with Zayd]. The accusative was preferred here because of conjoining the clause of ishtighāl to a verbal clause before it, namely His saying «يُدْخِلُ». al-Zubayr, Abān ibn ʿUthmān and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «والظَّالمون» in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate); it is the less preferred because of the lack of correspondence. Ibn Masʿūd read «وللظالمين» with the lām of the genitive. There are two aspects to it. The well-known one: «للظَّالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَعَدَّ» after it, and «لهم» is a tawkīd (emphasis). The second, which is very weak: it is of the ishtighāl type, on the basis that you imply a verb like the overt one and the noun is put in the genitive by a preposition, so we say «بزيدٍ مررتُ به», i.e. I passed by Zayd, I passed by him. What is known in the language of the Arabs is the school of the majority, namely implying an accusative-governing verb agreeing with the overt verb in meaning. If something like «بزيدٍ مَرَرْتُ به» occurs, it is counted as emphasis, not as ishtighāl.
